questions.answer: A transverse wave is a wave in which the displacement of particles is perpendicular to the direction of energy transfer. A longitudinal wave is a wave in which particle displacement is parallel to the direction of energy propagation.
accepted_alternatives: Oscillations may be used instead of particle displacement, and wave travel or propagation may be used instead of energy transfer.

marking_points.text: States that a transverse wave is a wave in which the displacement of particles is perpendicular to the direction of energy transfer.
States that a longitudinal wave is a wave in which particle displacement is parallel to the direction of energy propagation.

accepted_alternatives: Equivalent wording that separates local oscillation of the rope from travel of the disturbance or energy.
